title: Incident Ops Synthesis and Customer Commitment Kit
author: Marisol Chen
content:
Summary:
This document collates the core incident lifecycle guidance, runbook templates, on-call rotation patterns, game-day play outlines, and customer-facing status templates we use to fulfill commitments when Redwood experiences service disruptions. It is intended for SREs, service owners, customer success, and on-call engineers.

Scope and intent:
- Scope: Applies to all public-facing inference endpoints (hosted API, dedicated pools) and control-plane services that impact customer request routing, billing, or data access.
- Intent: Reduce time-to-stabilize, make customer communication predictable and clear, and ensure post-incident learning drives improvements to SLOs and runbooks.

Quick reference: roles and responsibilities
1) Incident Lead (IL) — generally the oncall SRE or service owner. Owns timeline, decisions, and customer brief cadence.
2) Bridge Operator — runs the war-room (Zoom/MS Teams), snapshots evidence, posts updates to the status page.
3) Tier-1 Responder — initial triage, short-term mitigations, tooling to mute noisy alerts.
4) Tier-2/3 Engineers — deep debugging, remediation, and config changes.
5) Customer Success Liaison — crafts external messaging and liaises with affected accounts.
6) Postmortem Owner — writes the retrospective, tracks action items.

Incident classification matrix (short):
- Sev 1: Global outage affecting >25% customers or system-level SLO breach >30 mins. Requires immediate IL, exec notification.
- Sev 2: Partial degradation impacting specific features or regions with measurable SLO regression. Notify affected customers within 60 min.
- Sev 3: Minor or isolated issues with limited customer impact; handled in normal oncall cadence.

Incident lifecycle (detailed run-loop):
1) Detection & initial triage (0-5 min)
   - Pager fires; Tier-1 responder acknowledges in 5 min.
   - Collect these 3 data points within first 10 minutes: symptom (error/latency), blast radius (tenants/regions), and possible choke points (GPU pool, autoscaler, network).
2) Mobilize bridge and assign roles (5-15 min)
   - IL opens bridge; tags owner on service and storage components.
   - Bridge Operator posts initial status: "Investigating — impact, affected regions, ETA for next update".
3) Contain (15-45 min)
   - Apply safe mitigations: scale up reserved pools, add read-only fallbacks, route traffic to alternate region/model variant.
   - If mitigation has service-level risk, IL must log decision & reason in bridge notes.
4) Stabilize (45 min — 4 hrs)
   - Confirm traffic and SLO trends returning to baseline.
   - Create short-term change (e.g., config toggles) with the SRE guardrail checklist.
5) Restore & validate (4 hrs — 24 hrs)
   - Run smoke tests and customer-impact tests. Confirm no regressions.
   - If customer-affecting, Customer Success Liaison prepares account-specific notes.
6) Close & postmortem (24 hrs — 7 days)
   - Postmortem drafted within 48 hours; final review and action items tracked in the oncall board.

Triage checklist (copyable):
- Acknowledge pager
- Snapshot metrics (latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, 5xx counts)
- Check autoscale and GPU pool health (node counts, GPU OOM logs)
- Query routing & traffic split (region, model variant)
- Identify any recent deploys or config changes
- Enable throttling/unassign noisy tenants if necessary

Runbook template (canonical) — paste into service runbooks and keep small:
- Title: <service-name> incident runbook
- Symptoms: <short list>
- Initial checks (commands):
  - curl -i https://svc.internal/health || echo "service down"
  - kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=<svc> --no-headers
  - rrdtool fetch /metrics/requests "LAST"
- Quick mitigations (ordered):
  1) Redirect traffic to healthy region: routerctl route set <svc> --region us-west-2
  2) Scale dedicated pool: redwoodctl pool scale --name dedicated-<svc> --replicas +2
  3) Toggle prefix cache bypass: redwoodctl cache update --service <svc> --mode bypass
- Escalation: if not resolved in 30 min escalate to service owner and SRE lead
- Post-incident tasks: add telemetry, add synthetic checks, schedule canary test

Operational guardrails and safe-change checklist (for oncall change approvals):
- Has the change been reviewed by the IL? (Y/N)
- Does this change risk customer data loss? (Y/N)
- Will the change roll back automatically if error rate increases? (Y/N)
- Is there a scheduled quiet window? (Y/N)
- Notify Customer Success if >10 customers affected.

On-call rotation design patterns (recommended):
- Primary/secondary weekly cadence: Primary is the responder for the week; secondary takes over bridge ops and after-hours mitigation approval.
- Follow-the-sun overlap windows: 0700–1000 PST and 1500–1800 PST to cross-handover knowledge.
- Two-week shadow apprenticeship for new oncall engineers with graded responsibilities.
- Rotation docs should include runbook links, oncall-level decision ladders, and a small playbook index.

Game day blueprint (90–120 min session):
- Objective: validate cross-region failover, KV cache warmup, and backup routing to model-variant fallbacks.
- Participants: SREs (2), service owners (2), Customer Success (1), Observability engineer (1).
- Pre-reqs: baseline synthetic pass, canary traffic generator configured, and a standby customer liaison.
- Exercise steps:
  1) Trigger simulated GPU pool OOM in us-east-1 (execution by infra engineer).
  2) Observe autoscaler response and confirm traffic spill to us-west-2.
  3) Validate prefix cache warmup in target region and measure p95 delta.
  4) Test customer comm template and time-to-first-notice.
- Scoring: time-to-bridge <=5 min, time-to-first-mitigation <=20 min, p95 recovery to within 2x baseline within 30 min.

Status page and customer communication templates
- Principles: be fast, factual, and actionable. Avoid speculation; give an ETA for next update. Use the phrase "investigating" until mitigation verified.

Template A — Initial public status (short):
Title: Degraded performance affecting inference endpoints\Impact: Some customers may experience increased latency or errors.\Current status: Investigating — we are seeing elevated error rates for traffic routed to us-east-1 queues.\Next update: in 30 minutes.
Advice for customers: If you use region pinned hosts, consider switching to us-west-2 as a temporary workaround. Contact support@redwood.ai for account-specific assistance.

Template B — Account-specific email (when known impact):
\Subject: Redwood status update — temporary performance degradation for <customer-name>\Hi <CS Rep> / <Customer Contact>,\We are investigating elevated error rates affecting requests for your account. Our engineers have applied a routing mitigation and are monitoring.\What we’re doing: scaled dedicated pool for your tenant and moved traffic to encrypted-us-west-2 nodes.\Action for you: no action required unless you continue to see errors. If you prefer, we can coordinate a manual failover at a scheduled time.\Estimated next update: <ETA>

Template C — Post-incident customer closing note and remediation offer:
\Subject: Incident resolved — summary and remediation options for <customer-name>\Hi <Customer Contact>,\Summary: On <date> we experienced a performance degradation caused by <root-cause>. The service was fully restored at <time>.\Impact: Your account experienced ~X% additional latency and Y failed requests during the incident window.\What we fixed: <short list of technical remediations>.\Compensation: We will credit <X>% of the affected usage billed in <month> per our SLA. Please let your CS rep know if you require additional evidence.\Next steps: we scheduled a targeted follow-up with your team to discuss longer-term mitigations.\nRegards,\Customer Success / Incident Response

Postmortem template (required fields):
- Title
- Incident ID
- Severity
- Start / End times (UTC)
- Affected services and customers
- Detecting signal(s)
- Root cause (one-paragraph)
- Timeline of events (minute-level bullets)
- Mitigations applied (short list)
- Corrective action(s) and owners (include ETA)
- Follow-up validations and telemetry to add
- Blameless summary and learnings

Example timeline excerpt (format):
- 2026-02-10T14:03Z — Pager triggered: router p95 > 1500ms
- 2026-02-10T14:05Z — Bridge opened; IL assigned: @marisol. Initial post to status page.
- 2026-02-10T14:16Z — Scale-up of dedicated pool in us-west-2 completed.
- 2026-02-10T14:42Z — p95 returned to baseline; monitoring stable.

SLOs and evidence collection (minimum):
- SLOs to monitor: request p50/p95/p99, 5xx rate, queue depth, and head-of-line latency.
- Evidence archive: bridge log (transcript), snapshots of dashboards, relevant kube logs (kubectl logs with timestamps), and saved tracer spans (jaeger link).
- Retention: put incident evidence into the incident-bucket with path: s3://incident-evidence/<incident-id>/ and tag the runbook entry.

Escalation matrix (short bullets):
- If unresolved after 30 min: escalate to service owner and SRE lead.
- If unresolved after 3 hours OR customer credit threshold met: notify CTO and Customer Success SVP.

SLA credit decision ladder (summary):
- If cross-tenant SLO > 30 minutes in a billing month, trigger auto-review for credit.
- Manual exceptions handled by Finance & Legal in coordination with CS.

Runbook hygiene and governance:
- Runbooks must be <700 words and contain 3 quick mitigations.
- Each service runbook is reviewed quarterly by the owner and during each major release.
- Retire or archive runbooks older than 18 months unless owner reaffirms relevance.

Appendix: useful CLI snippets and queries
- Basic health: curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health | jq .
- Resource checks: redwoodctl nodes list --region=us-east-1 --format=json | jq '.nodes | length'
- Traces: jaeger query --service <svc> --start <ISO-8601> --end <ISO-8601>

Appendix: decision record for customer notifications (short)
- Decision: Use conservative, repeated short updates (every 30–60 minutes) rather than infrequent long updates.
- Rationale: Frequent updates reduce inbound support load and increase customer trust.

Contact matrix (oncall distribution):
- Primary oncall: weekly rotation; backup: weekly rotation offset by one. For critical holidays, create a 2-person escalation pair.
